card.title: MARA
card.subtitle: MARA is a challenge-based platform to acquire talent, building the new standard of talent acquisition. I co-founded it with three teammates inside the H-FARM ecosystem. Three challenges shipped, 200+ students onboarded. Live on marachallenge.com.

interior.headline: Beyond the CV.
interior.hook: The CV had a good run. But in a world where AI and transformative forces are constantly reshaping what work looks like, a list of past titles no longer tells you what someone can actually do. MARA was born from that disconnect. A talent acquisition platform where companies publish real challenges, students compete to solve them in focused sprints, and the best solution wins. No CVs. Just proof of work.

sections.label: The origin
sections.body:
Four H-FARM College master's students (Michele Gualano, Alessandro Della Rocca, Rita Zhubi, Alessandro Pio Alvigi) were two months into the program when the pattern became impossible to ignore. Even in a place built for entrepreneurship, the disconnect was a blocker. The person sitting next to you might have the next big idea; you might be exactly who they need to make it real. But there was no bridge.

The pivot moment came at H-FARM's Career Day, already different from any university fair we'd attended. Students weren't handing out CVs. They were in open labs, working alongside companies, solving problems in real time. That was it. Not another job board. A platform that brings companies, students, and universities together around a shared challenge. Already inside the H-FARM Startup Center Pre-Accelerator, we had the space, mentorship, and momentum to make it real.

sections.label: How MARA works
sections.body: A B2Education platform built on three actors. Students work on real company challenges and build a portfolio of proof, not promises. Companies find proven talent already observed under pressure. Universities activate their ecosystems and strengthen experiential learning. The flow is five steps: pre-challenge consulting, brief design, two-week sprint, jury evaluation, talent pipeline. The best solution wins, evaluated against predefined KPIs. All submitted work transfers as full IP to the company.

sections.label: Proof of work, not paper claims
sections.body: AI and the rewriting of every job role are making a list of past experiences less and less sufficient. The unit of evidence is shifting from "what I claim I can do" to "what I shipped". MARA structures that shift. The jury scores on Idea Originality, Team Dynamics, Solution Viability, Presentation Craft, and Brief Coherence — observable signals from a real engagement.

sections.label: First time live
sections.body: MARA's first real test ran on H-ACK, the H-FARM hackathon co-organized with YouTuber Jakidale. The platform didn't just hold — it ran the event end-to-end: 157 participants, 30 teams, 6 judges, all operating inside the MARA workspace to manage tasks, collaborate, and submit their final work. Rita Zhubi's team won the "Robot Companion" brief and received the first Soulbound credential, MARA-2026-0043. For a platform that launched just days before, that's not a pilot. That's a proof of concept.

sections.label: The first real company challenge
sections.body: Shortly after H-ACK, the first real corporate challenge landed on MARA: a global hospitality group chose H-FARM College students to tackle a complex brief about a new generation of travelers who blur the lines between work, life, and play. H-FARM College is running the challenge. MARA is the platform powering it. The winning team earns a seat alongside the company's leadership at a top-tier industry event. Not a case study. A real brief, from a real company, with real stakes.

sections.label: What is live
sections.body: marachallenge.com — modern web stack, Polygon-anchored credentialing, AI woven through the platform from brief generation to evaluation. Frictionless for the participant.

sections.label: What's next
sections.body: H-ACK was chapter one. MARA's mission is changing the hiring world with proof of work, and 157 students that weekend were just the beginning. What comes next are real companies, real challenges, and a generation of students who won't need a CV to prove their worth. H-FARM College and the MARA team are extending the platform to other ongoing programs across the college; year-1 plan targets 18 challenges across three intakes. Featured by H-FARM College in April 2026 ("Beyond the CV").

interior.credits: Co-founders: Michele Gualano · Alessandro Della Rocca · Rita Zhubi · Alessandro Pio Alvigi · marachallenge.com

card.title: Slow Landscape
card.subtitle: An AI-driven de-seasonalization campaign for Le Vigne al Castello (Andria, near Castel del Monte). Built around Federico II, a Midjourney-generated digital host inspired by Frederick II of Swabia, the medieval emperor who commissioned the castle.

interior.headline: An off-season campaign for a small Puglia hotel, built around a 13th-century emperor.
interior.hook: Five-week brief inside the H-FARM College × Università di Foggia program. The client: Le Vigne al Castello, a new venture in Puglia, five kilometres from Castel del Monte. The problem: Puglia tourism collapses outside July and August. Our move: build Federico II, a Midjourney-generated digital host inspired by Frederick II of Swabia, and design three off-season commercial packages around him.

sections.label: The seasonal problem
sections.body: Puglia tourism is hyper-polarized: July and August spike, winter goes flat. Andria, the town that hosts the property, registered 24,819 arrivals and 52,158 overnight stays in 2024. The hotel runs high fixed costs against this curve.

sections.label: Federico II as digital host
sections.body: Frederick II of Swabia was the Holy Roman Emperor who commissioned Castel del Monte. The site sits five kilometres from the property. Our avatar Federico II becomes Genius Loci, the spirit of the place. Romantic escapes are framed as invitations to court. Wine experiences become treasures of his land. Corporate retreats are the new court that withdraws to think.

sections.label: Three commercial packages
sections.body: Romantic Retreat at around €205: one night in a Suite, aperitivo at Cantine Torrevento, Wine Painting Lab, four-course dinner at Osteria Ottolune, late check-out. Taste of Tradition & History at around €300: two nights in a Junior Suite, Nero di Troia masterclass, pasta workshop, Castel del Monte tour, e-bike rental. Smart Business Package: one night Deluxe, Blending Game team-building masterclass, meeting room, gala banquet, airport transfer.

sections.label: The AI production pipeline
sections.body: Midjourney for image generation, confirmed by the actual prompts in our deck (--ar 16:9 --style raw --v 6). Video pipeline using motion flags in the same prompt format. Generic LLMs for bilingual captions and the discorsivo narration script per slide. The team output: a 25-slide strategy deck, an 18-slide Italian visual deck with full prompts, four YouTube Shorts demos, and an omnichannel media plan across Instagram (Reels, Link Stickers, Link-in-Bio) and TikTok (10–30s short-form).

sections.label: Why it matters
sections.body: A photo shoot on Mars costs the same as one in New York when the model is Midjourney. The team behind the persona produces continuous premium content on a campaign budget that would otherwise buy two human photo shoots. The virtual influencer market sits at $9.75B in 2024 with a 38% CAGR. The right vehicle for an off-season hospitality brand without a megastudio budget.

interior.credits: Team 2 · Slow Landscape · H-FARM College × Università di Foggia · Client: Apulia Hotel Le Vigne al Castello · Andria
pull_quotes: We're not fighting the sea in August. We're winning when the sea slows down.

visual_identity.treatment: Sand + terracotta + Mediterranean ochre. Serif display for the slow, deliberate cadence; sans body to keep the strategic content crisp. Lands as Puglia, not generic Mediterranean.

card.title: GameBL
card.subtitle: A 2D adventure game built to raise awareness about gambling addiction. Cartoon-dark style. PM + Creative Director. Apple Academy 2025, selected into IdeaSolution Naples incubator.

interior.headline: GameBL, a 2D adventure about gambling.
interior.hook: GameBL makes players reflect on gambling addiction, through a cartoon-dark visual language, a symbolic protagonist, and levels where obstacles get more alluring the further you go. Apple Developer Academy, Naples, Feb 2025. Selected into the IdeaSolution Naples incubator.

sections.label: Premise
sections.body: Not entertainment as escape, entertainment as recognition. GameBL is a 2D adventure with a gripping, deliberately uneasy tone. The protagonist has a simple, symbolic appearance; the player walks them through levels where obstacles and temptations get more alluring the further you progress. The thing you're warning against is the thing the game makes you feel.

sections.label: My role
sections.body: PM and creative director. I designed every visual asset in the game by hand in Keynote, characters, level art, UI, dice, death counter, menu screens. The team handled engineering and game logic; I owned the look, the narrative arc, and the sound design.

sections.label: Build
sections.body: Mobile-first iOS build. Custom character design, cartoon-dark environments (silhouette landscapes, storm-cloud backdrops), original soundtrack, prototyped against real playtest sessions across the Academy cycle. Visual and sound identity built in-house to keep a tight, recognizable feel from menu to last level.

sections.label: Outcome
sections.body: Selected into the IdeaSolution Naples incubator program, the team's output recognized as something that could grow beyond a coursework artifact.

sections.label: What I learned
sections.body: How fast a small team ships when the creative director is also the producer. And how a serious topic earns its weight when the form matches the content, cartoon-dark turned out to be exactly the register a gambling-awareness story needed to land without being either grim or preachy.

card.title: Terra Stage
card.subtitle: Crowd safety + offline-first fan experience for live events, powered by Copernicus satellite data. CASSINI Hackathon Italy, Oct 2025.

interior.headline: Event-risk maps from space, built in 48 hours at CASSINI.
interior.hook: TerraStage is the entry my team built at the CASSINI Hackathon Italy in October 2025: a B2B platform that gives event hosts and attendees risk intelligence derived from Copernicus and Galileo satellite data. Two phases. The first plans the venue using SAR, NDVI, multispectral imagery. The second navigates the venue on the day, offline-first, using Galileo positioning.

sections.label: Problem
sections.body: Outdoor events break for predictable, satellite-observable reasons: ground saturation, vegetation hazards, dust storms, crowd flow choke points. The organisers and the people in attendance both lack the same thing: a layered map of what the territory is actually doing on the day.

sections.label: Phase 1, Copernicus Risk Map (Hosts)
sections.body: Before the event: pull Copernicus satellite data — soil moisture, vegetation/NDVI risk, atmospheric conditions. Render the site as a layered risk surface. The host plans the layout against actual ground conditions instead of a generic terrain map.

sections.label: Phase 2, Galileo Offline Map (Attendees)
sections.body: On the day: Galileo high-accuracy positioning works without cell data (which collapses at large gatherings). The attendee app caches the venue map locally and uses Galileo for fine-grained location. Crowd safety without dependence on the cell network.

sections.label: Why this works
sections.body: Proactive safety: prevent issues with space-grade data before day one. Offline-proof fan experience: guidance and reconnection even when the network drops. Evidence you can show: a dashboard and an ESG report stakeholders trust. Simple for hosts. Simple for fans. High impact, low friction.

interior.credits: Team: Alessandro Pio Alvigi, Allegra Moscon (pitch lead), [+ teammates to confirm] · CASSINI Hackathon Italy · H-FARM, October 2025

visual_identity.treatment: Mission-control aesthetic, near-black, phosphor green, monospace display. Echoes the data substrate without becoming sci-fi cosplay.

card.title: Leafy
card.subtitle: An iOS app that gamifies plant recognition, point your camera, the AI identifies, the game turns naming plants into a habit. Apple Academy, Challenge 2, Nov 2024.

interior.headline: Gamifying plant recognition, point, identify, collect.
interior.hook: Leafy turns plant recognition into a small game. Camera feeds an AI vision API; the model identifies; the app rewards the act of paying attention to plants. Apple Developer Academy Challenge 2, two-week sprint with the Pasta Ammiscata crew, November 2024.

sections.label: Brief
sections.body: Apple Developer Academy Challenge 2, small cross-functional team, two weeks, ship an iOS app end-to-end on a sustainability brief. We picked plant literacy: a camera-based scanner that identifies a small set of common plants and teaches you something about each one. Scope was the design constraint, four plants, one scanner, one dictionary, one onboarding flow. The discipline was deciding what NOT to make.

sections.label: Brand
sections.body: Named the app Leafy and built a wordmark that grows. The “e” holds a tiny seed that sprouts across five frames into a full pair of leaves, used as splash animation and as a recurring beat in the onboarding. The metaphor is the product: small thing, given attention, grows. A logo that does the brand’s job rather than sit beside it.

sections.label: My role
sections.body: Project manager + branding. As PM: kept the cross-functional team aligned across developers and designers, milestones, scope calls, prioritization through a two-week sprint. As branding lead: gave the app its name, designed the growing-sprout wordmark, set the tone of voice, and held the brand spine across every screen the team shipped.

sections.label: Build
sections.body: SwiftUI on iOS. Camera-driven plant scanner backed by an AI vision API that handles the recognition (we didn't train our own model, the design move was using a hosted classifier well, not building one). On the front: a four-plant collectible dictionary (Cactus, Daisy, Rosemary, Cyclamen), an onboarding flow with an animated growing-sprout wordmark, a plant detail view, settings. Original hand-drawn illustrations for every plant in a single coherent style.

sections.label: What I learned
sections.body: Two weeks is short enough that every cut is visible. The discipline isn't in shipping more, it's in deciding what not to make. And: gamification only works if the underlying activity is already a tiny bit interesting. Plants are. Naming them is. The game just lowers the friction to start.

interior.credits: Team "Pasta Ammiscata": Alessandro Pio Alvigi (PM · Branding), Roberta Filaseta, Francesco "Kekko" Romeo, Can Dindar, Diego Moreno, Cinzia Ferrara · Apple Developer Academy, Naples

card.title: EmotionPlaylist
card.subtitle: Trained a CoreML emotion classifier with Create ML to learn how the pipeline works end-to-end.

interior.headline: CoreML × Create ML, training the pipeline end-to-end.
interior.hook: EmotionPlaylist is the iOS app I built around a custom-trained CoreML emotion classifier. The point wasn't a polished product, it was understanding Create ML as a training environment and CoreML as the on-device inference runtime. The pipeline became a working app.

sections.label: Create ML
sections.body: Used Create ML on macOS to train a custom emotion classifier from scratch: assemble a dataset, define the task, run training, inspect accuracy across emotion categories, debug where the model gets confused. Iterated through versions, ship the trained classifier as a CoreML model.

sections.label: CoreML
sections.body: The trained model exports to CoreML and runs fully on-device, no API calls, no cloud, no data leaving the phone. SwiftUI app feeds text or speech into the same inference pipeline; the model returns an emotion; AVSpeechSynthesizer reads it back for VoiceOver users.

sections.label: What I learned
sections.body: Three things. Most of the ML work is in the data, not the model. Shipping a model is its own discipline, latency, battery, privacy. AI literacy doesn't start with using AI; it starts with training something small enough that you can see where it breaks.

interior.credits: Solo build · Alessandro Pio Alvigi · Apple Developer Academy, Naples · Dec 2024

visual_identity.treatment: Deep eggplant canvas with a soft lavender ink and warm magenta accent, emotional and musical, not utilitarian. Serif display gives the headline weight without becoming clinical.

card.title: Lux Collective

interior.headline: A five-week challenge by The Lux Collective, run end-to-end on MARA. My team also competed.
interior.hook: The Lux Collective is a global hotel management company headquartered in Mauritius, brands LUX*, SALT, SOCIO, Tamassa, 18 resorts operating, 16 in pipeline across Sharjah, Bali, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Oman. From 18 March to 21 April 2026, they ran a branded student challenge on MARA, the platform I co-founded. The prize: lunch with the CEO and CCO at World Travel Market London, plus press conference attendance on 4 November 2026. My team competed in the challenge. The MARA team hosted it.

sections.label: The brief
sections.body: Work, Play, and Purpose: Empowering the Social Nomads. Redesign SOCIO's social spaces with USPs that differentiate from The Hoxton, 25hours, Mama Shelter and Yotel. 4–5 person H-FARM teams. 20–30 slide deck plus 7-minute pitch. Winning team assigns all IP perpetually, free of charge, to The Lux Collective.

sections.label: How MARA ran it
sections.body: Registration on marachallenge.com. Brief access through the platform. Submission flow through Google Drive. Checkpoint meetings on Cisco Webex. Four mentor sessions: the brief itself (24 March), an AI and Creative Tech workshop (31 March), an Experience Journey session (7 April), a deck review (14 April). Pre-selection by TLC on 20 April. sections.label: Our team's concept: Permission
sections.body: Every brand built the hardware of social space. None built the software, the rituals, rhythms, signals that tell people how to inhabit those spaces together. Our concept: Permission. Designed for the moment before connection. Two personas: Marta needs permission to not engage. Alex needs permission to approach. The competitive teardown of The Hoxton, 25hours, Mama Shelter exposed where each one underbuilt this layer.

sections.label: Why this is the real proof point
sections.body: A real global hotel group, with verifiable brands and a CEO-tier prize, ran a 5-week commercial-grade challenge end-to-end on a platform I co-founded. The IP-transfer term (winning team assigns all rights to TLC) tells you the engagement was not academic. This is exactly the kind of case study MARA needs as it goes to market, Want these challenges in your university? Get in touch.

card.title: H2H
card.subtitle: A personal-safety app that works without internet. Bluetooth Low Energy mesh sends encrypted SOS + GPS to nearby members. Apple Academy, Oct 2025.

interior.headline: When the cell tower drops, the phones still talk to each other.
interior.hook: H2H is a personal-safety app for the moments when there is no network: hiking out of coverage, festival crowds saturating the local cell, earthquakes that take the towers down. The phones form a peer-to-peer mesh: each device discovers nearby devices over Bluetooth Low Energy and Wi-Fi P2P, and an SOS broadcast hops device-to-device until it reaches someone with coverage who can call for help. No server. No internet. No router.

sections.label: The concept
sections.body: Most emergency apps assume one thing the user often does not have: a working connection. We inverted the assumption. When there is no network, treat the other phones in the area as the network.

sections.label: What mesh networking is, in this app
sections.body: iOS Multipeer Connectivity discovers nearby devices over a mix of Bluetooth Low Energy, Wi-Fi Direct, and infrastructure Wi-Fi. Each H2H instance is both client and relay. When you press the SOS button, your phone broadcasts a packet with GPS coordinates and a help payload. Devices in range receive it, display the alert, and re-broadcast. The packet hops device-to-device until it reaches someone with coverage, who relays it out to emergency contacts.

sections.label: Privacy by design
sections.body: Coordinates and identity are encrypted at the device. Devices in the mesh that aren't the recipient relay an opaque packet they cannot read. No central server stores location history. The mesh exists only while the SOS is active.

sections.label: Interface
sections.body: One screen, one red button. Coordinates visible at the top so the user can read them out loud if needed. SOS message log in red at the bottom showing what has been broadcast and what has been acknowledged. No menus, no settings, no learning curve. The whole UX assumes the user is already in trouble.

sections.label: What I learned
sections.body: Pioneering communication tech under hard constraints (no network, low battery, high stakes) sharpened a different muscle than shipping marketing comms. Privacy-aware design isn't a privacy policy, it's protocol choices. And leading a team through a demanding technical brief is its own creative discipline.

interior.credits: Team "Daiquiri" · Alessandro Pio Alvigi (Communication · Creative Director) · [+ teammates to confirm] · Apple Developer Academy, Naples

visual_identity.treatment: Pure white + black ink + emergency red. The interior should read like the app reads: nothing decorative, one urgent affordance, clear copy. Sans across the board.

card.title: Fidus
card.subtitle: A mobile-first subscription app for first-time Italian dog owners. Training, insurance, and an AI assistant in one product. I built the MVP across nine Claude-assisted code generation cycles. Co-built with Rita. Origin: my own French Bulldog, Asso.

interior.headline: I built this from inside the problem.
interior.hook: Fidus did not start from a market analysis. It started from a need that was mine, when I welcomed Asso into a life that I quickly discovered had no instructions for what came next. Around 600,000 Italians get their first puppy every year. I built the MVP across nine Claude-assisted iteration cycles, co-built alongside Rita with our two dogs as the first and most stubborn quality assurance team.

sections.label: The problem
sections.body: Italy has roughly 8 million dogs and only 22% are insured. Sweden is at 90%. The serviceable obtainable market is €17.1 million. The target persona is Sofia Romano, 29, a marketing coordinator in Milan, anxious first-time owner of a Golden Retriever puppy named Luna. She does not need another product page. She needs the next step.

sections.label: What I built
sections.body: A mobile-first product that bundles a 52-week training curriculum, insurance through partner insurers UnipolSai and Generali (10–15% affiliate commission, no revenue share), and Fidus AI, a Google Gemini layer conditioned on a proprietary breed-specialised knowledge base. The killer feature: multimodal extraction of vet invoices into a structured claim object, pre-filled into the partner insurer's template. Thirty-to-sixty-day claim cycles become a 3-minute guided interaction.

sections.label: How I built it
sections.body: Nine iterative Claude-assisted code generation cycles. Each cycle layered a new capability: EN translation, premium visual identity, flat tab navigation, insurance landing, fullscreen modal overlays, Daily Hub refinement, paw cursor, type migration from Lexend to Montserrat, React component refactor. Stack: React 19 with TypeScript on Vite, Tailwind, Framer Motion, Google Generative AI SDK, Supabase (EU region), Stripe web checkout outside Apple's IAP under the DMA exemption.

sections.label: Pricing and GTM
sections.body: Three tiers: Bronze €16.90/mo, Silver €33.90/mo, Gold €49.90/mo, with per-tier AI inference caps. Phase 1 spends €1,550/mo across vet clinics, pet shops, breeders, QR cards at point of adoption. Phase 2 layers paid social and SEM at €4,900/mo. Total six-month budget €19,350. Targets: 2,000 downloads, 5% trial-to-paid by month 3, CAC under €20. First commercial wedge: Campania, with Zoomiguana as the inaugural retail partner.

sections.label: Compliance posture
sections.body: GDPR Article 25 (Privacy by Design) and Article 32. IVASS Regolamento 40/2018: operates as affiliate distributor, not regulated intermediary. RUI registration is a Y2 milestone. DMA exemption is the reason Stripe checkout sits outside Apple's IAP. The MVP is real, the architecture is defensible, and the people who are about to use it are people I know.

interior.credits: Builder: Alessandro Pio Alvigi · Co-builder: Rita · QA team: Asso (French Bulldog) and Rita's dog · H-FARM MSc Strategic Plan v6 (April 2026)
pull_quotes: Each design choice that survived the nine prototype cycles is a choice I would have wanted to find as a first-time owner.

visual_identity.treatment: Cream + deep navy ink, heritage Italian feel, fitting Latin name and the trust the category requires. The winged-bulldog crest reads as institutional without being stuffy.

card.subtitle: The first B2B marketplace born from Sardinia's Mercato Ortofrutticolo di Sestu. Pre-launch. Incubated through the H-FARM Startup Center Pre-Accelerator. Commercial specifics under NDA.

interior.headline: Designing how a wholesale market enters the digital age.
interior.hook: Agromercato.com is the first B2B marketplace born from the heart of Sardinia's Mercato Ortofrutticolo all'Ingrosso di Sestu. The platform extends the physical market into the digital channel without replacing it: six founding wholesalers connected to professional buyers across the region. My focus is acquisition design — how to bring a buyer audience that lives on WhatsApp into a new tool without forcing the migration. Currently incubated through the H-FARM Startup Center Pre-Accelerator. Commercial specifics under NDA.

sections.label: What it is
sections.body: Agromercato.com, “Il mercato di sempre, nel futuro di tutti.” The first B2B marketplace born inside the Mercato Agroalimentare della Sardegna (Sestu) — part of Italmercati, the national network of 22 Italian wholesale agri-food markets that together move 7.1 million metric tons per year and serve 7 million annual visitors. The platform connects the market's wholesalers to professional buyers across the region (ristoratori, negozianti, strutture ricettive, operatori della distribuzione). Mobile apps on iOS and Android.

sections.label: What I worked on
sections.body: Acquisition design. How the platform reaches a buyer audience that prefers messaging over apps. WhatsApp-first community, trusted-referral chains through early adopters, and phygital touchpoints inside the physical marketplace.

sections.label: Customer research
sections.body: Customer research with the market's buyer audience surfaced a clear signal that shaped the whole acquisition strategy. Specific data under NDA, but the direction was unambiguous: the existing behavior of this audience pointed toward WhatsApp as the right entry channel, and to the agent layer on top of it.

sections.label: The strategic insight
sections.body: Cultural barrier is bigger than tech barrier. In a market where buyers already do business through voice and messaging, the move was not to push them onto a new app but to meet them inside the tool they were already using. The platform should ride on existing behavior, not fight it.

sections.label: Where it sits now
sections.body: Pre-launch. The platform and apps are live (agromercato.com, iOS + Android); full commercial activation is ongoing. Incubated through the H-FARM Startup Center Pre-Accelerator. Specific go-to-market figures remain under NDA until launch.
